goal: Software as the instructions that tell hardware what to do: sort hardware and software cards, name kinds of software by job, then trace one click from input, through the software, to the screen on the system-diagram
note: Anchor: the teacher clicks "draw a circle" on the class screen and the class asks what did the work. After the hook, the retrieval task: place two pictured parts on the system-diagram as input or output (grade 2), then the software box is added. Device day: one device per pair (15 for 30), with the few-device stations, one-screen and no-device versions the unit plan writes; the last four minutes save or print work, shut devices and collect papers; devices are carried with two hands and cords stay behind the table. Paper path: the card sort and a printed click-to-circle strip traced with a pencil. Exit ticket: one new task, what the software does between input and output. Ours (no base lesson).

goal: How a message reaches another place: act out a message passed through a chain of devices and a helper, draw it as a network-diagram with a labeled cloud meaning many other people's computers, then see how people use devices to find information and to talk
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace: one task traced on the system-diagram (day 1). Act-out at a walk in a cleared room, the message card passed hand to hand. Then on one screen: a teacher-led search for a fact (nothing typed by a child) and a pictured video call with family far away. Paper path: a printed strip of the search, step by step. Candidate kept: networks joined into a network of networks inside this day, zero added days. Base: archived Year 3 "Connecting computers" lessons 4 to 6 and Year 4 "The Internet" lessons 1, 2 and 4, rewritten in our words; credit once. Leans on an unloaded source (later.csv L149): the archived base is placed from its unit pages only.

goal: Which details in a pretend profile, post or online game could show who a person is or where they live, what is safe to share and with whom, and one post rewritten to be safer
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace: a pretend post, what happens next and to whom (grade 2). Paper pretend pages only, with the "you won a prize, type your address" pop-up. Sensitive: online safety and personal information; the teacher page carries health's "If a student tells you something" steps word for word; no card asks for a real name, screen name, school or street, and no task asks what devices, games or accounts a child has at home. Base: archived Year 4 "The Internet" lesson 3, rewritten in our words; credit once. Leans on an unloaded source (later.csv L149): the archived base is placed from its unit pages only.

goal: Weigh a new technology in family life (a video call with relatives) and a widely used community system (a map with route directions) on the benefit-risk-chart, with family and community rows and one thing a person can do about a harm
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace: one helps and one hurts for a pictured tool on the chart (grade 2). Society day: the teacher page gives two brief views of the system with one dated source each (one on who the map helps, one on a harm such as a shared location, each from a public agency or news page, picked and dated when the cards are written); the family and town scenes are invented for practice and marked so. Sensitive: the map's harms (a family whose location is shared) are told as things that can happen to anyone, never about a classmate's family. Evidence: a short written claim with a reason tied to the two views. Ours (no base lesson).

goal: Machine learning on a training set: the class acts as a sorter trained on insect and spider cards with few side-view spiders, is tested on ten new cards, gets more side-view examples, is tested again, and tallies right answers before and after to say why it changed
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace: which new card will an uneven sorter get wrong (grade 2). The sorter decides only by the yes or no feature questions the class writes from the training cards (for one: can you see eight legs? are there two body parts?); a child who knows the answer another way keeps it for the tally. Side-view spiders show fewer legs, so the first questions miss them. Unplugged: the class is the sorter, which meets E3-ALG-ML-02 in full (its boundary asks students to observe, not train). An optional one-screen sorter trained by the teacher may show the same, nothing stored or sent. The sorter's mistakes are about pictures of insects and spiders, never people or faces. The teacher supplies the training and test cards; grade 5 (days 22 and 23) has pairs build and split their own sets. Ours (no base lesson).
